title: AI papers on arXiv — Tuesday, 27 October 2026 batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This ordering is inferred from dated third-party Hugging Face Daily Papers upvotes after filtering for the official 27 October batch; citation evidence for these recent preprints is limited and was not used to rank them.

sections.title: Trajectory2Gym: Decision-Grounded Compositional Interaction Synthesis for Tool-Use Agents
sections.abstract: Trajectory2Gym constructs tool-use training interactions that cover underrepresented dependencies and only supervises decisions supported by the agent-visible history.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 16.9–29.8 percentage-point gains in the equal-weight mean across Tau1, Tau2, and BFCL over tested Qwen3 scales, with strongest gains on stateful and multi-turn interactions.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported results are on three tool-use benchmarks and Qwen3 scales; transfer to other agent families and live tool environments is not established.
sections.ranking_evidence: 121 upvotes in the Tuesday 27 October Hugging Face Daily Papers list, the highest count on that dated list; third-party attention signal, not an arXiv popularity statistic.

sections.title: StreamVibe: Proactive Video Agents for Evolving User Intent
sections.abstract: StreamVibe combines a benchmark, streaming vision-language model, and persistent-state harness to infer implicit user intent and adapt responses as that intent changes.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a 10.7% improvement in response timing and answer quality over baselines and a further 12.3% gain in proactive interaction from the StreamVibe harness.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors note that the benchmark does not yet capture richer co-evolution of user intent and environment over longer horizons.
sections.ranking_evidence: 98 upvotes in the Tuesday daily list, second-highest; the paper reports a 4.1K-sample benchmark and sustained-interaction experiments.

sections.title: InteractiveWorld: A Verifiable Human-Centric Environment for Building Better Interactive MLLM Assistants
sections.abstract: InteractiveWorld simulates closed-loop assistance in which an MLLM instructs a human actor who acts in a changing scene, and provides a 120-task benchmark with state-based rewards.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that even their strongest tested model reaches at most 20% on long-horizon Guidance and 25% on Planning tasks.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors identify human-agent realism and additional real environments as future work; benchmark outcomes are not yet a substitute for deployment with diverse real users.
sections.ranking_evidence: 71 upvotes in the Tuesday daily list, third among listed papers; the benchmark evaluates 12 frontier MLLMs and includes a human-agent study.

sections.title: WorldCast: World-Consistent Character Video Generation with Large-Angle Camera Control
sections.abstract: WorldCast combines explicit 3D geometric guidance with geometry-aligned memory attention to preserve character appearance and identity during large-angle camera motion in generated video.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report accurate camera-trajectory following while preserving character geometry, appearance, and identity on the CLACT benchmark.
sections.unique_caveat: The evaluation is focused on character-centric video and the proposed large-angle camera benchmark; results do not establish generalization to other video-generation domains.
sections.ranking_evidence: 40 upvotes in the Tuesday daily list, fourth-highest; the authors introduce a dedicated large-angle camera-trajectory dataset.

sections.title: Spatial Audio Generation and Editing with Executable Plans and Self-Distilling Transfusion
sections.abstract: AMBIT uses executable scene plans and a shared Transfusion model for first-order ambisonics audio generation and editing, with on-policy self-distillation for planning and rendering.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improvements in generation content and spatial quality, instruction-guided editing fidelity, and preservation of unedited sources over compared baselines.
sections.unique_caveat: The work targets first-order ambisonics and its reported speech/music/sound evaluation; broader spatial formats and downstream listening use cases are not established by the abstract.
sections.ranking_evidence: 28 upvotes in the Tuesday daily list, tied for fifth; the paper tests speech, music, and sound and is cross-listed in cs.AI.

sections.title: DynaFlow: Learning Free-Form Multi-Agent Orchestration
sections.abstract: DynaFlow trains a main agent to synthesize executable workflows that coordinate fixed sub-agents through sequential or parallel calls, structured information exchange, and verification.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 88.08% overall accuracy in Forced mode with Qwen3.5-27B, 10.90 percentage points above their strongest evaluated baseline.
sections.unique_caveat: The method keeps all sub-agents fixed and improves the orchestrator; it does not establish gains when executor capabilities also change.
sections.ranking_evidence: 28 upvotes in the Tuesday daily list, tied with AMBIT; results cover six benchmarks and a same-backbone comparison.

sections.title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
sections.abstract: This work presents a systems-level framework for understanding digital work agents through persistence, openness, capability families, and joint model/harness optimization.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose a work-centric taxonomy covering persistence, openness, five task forms, five capability families, and approaches to model and harness optimization.
sections.unique_caveat: This is primarily a systems perspective and synthesis of existing methods rather than a single controlled benchmark result; its framework needs validation across deployed work settings.
sections.ranking_evidence: 22 upvotes in the Tuesday daily list; it organizes work-agent capabilities and evaluation around verifiable work outcomes and links code.

sections.title: Eat Your Precision: Precision Objective Mitigates Reward Hacking in Rubric-based RL
sections.abstract: FORK augments rubric-based reinforcement learning with a precision objective that penalizes unnecessary or factually incorrect response units alongside rubric coverage.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved precision and response length with similar rubric coverage, and higher win rates on RubricHub-Medical and HealthBench against a recall-based reward.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported win-rate evidence is from medical response benchmarks and relies on rubric necessity and factual-correctness judgments; transfer to other domains and grader reliability remain open.
sections.ranking_evidence: 19 upvotes in the Tuesday daily list; the authors report benchmark comparisons for precision and coverage and provide a code link.

sections.title: World-in-Context: Interactive Video World Modeling with In-Context Conditioning
sections.abstract: World-in-Context represents view, action, and camera controls as explicit tokens in shared attention and models temporal transitions accumulated from prior controls.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that the 5B model matches 22B EchoWM on WBench navigation (81.5 vs. 81.6) and reaches 93.8% perspective-switching success, compared with 18.8% for existing 5B baselines.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported comparisons are tied to WBench and the tested model sizes; transfer to physical control or broader interactive environments is not established.
sections.ranking_evidence: 17 upvotes in the Tuesday daily list; the paper reports navigation and perspective-switching measures on WBench.

sections.title: Δτ-Bench: Pushing Agents Toward a Moving Capability
sections.abstract: Δτ-Bench tests adaptation of procedural knowledge as tool ecosystems change and introduces Steward to maintain skills and provision tools during execution.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 42.3% task success for the strongest tested model or harness and higher success across ecosystem changes with lower skill-maintenance overhead for Steward.
sections.unique_caveat: The benchmark uses capability-preserving transformations to create successive ecosystem states; behavior under live, uncontrolled tool changes remains to be established.
sections.ranking_evidence: 15 upvotes in the Tuesday daily list; cross-listed in four core AI categories and evaluates 1,588 multi-turn tasks across 42 domains and six ecosystem states.

sections.title: Qwen-Image-PE: Learning Visual Design for Text-to-Image Prompt Enhancement
sections.abstract: Qwen-Image-PE trains prompt enhancers for visual design using caption-based supervised learning and groupwise image-reward reinforcement learning.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a 7.81-point gain on Qwen-Image-Bench for Qwen-Image-PE-397B and say the 9B model outperforms evaluated baselines, with gains on four additional text-to-image backbones.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported improvements concern prompt enhancement and visual-design benchmarks; the abstract does not establish gains for arbitrary image-generation workflows or user populations.
sections.ranking_evidence: 15 upvotes in the Tuesday daily list, tied with Δτ-Bench; source-list order breaks the tie. The paper reports cross-backbone evaluation and releases a 9B model.
